The project in 1 minute

What I set out to design

Brief

First-time UX and core flow for an AI-agent-led threat removal platform.

My role

Research, PRD, flows, UI and a clickable prototype.

Deliverables

OnboardingFirst visitFirst findingInvestigate & approve500+ threats a day
Setup to first scan result~5 min
Daily threats → human decisions527 → 6
Actions sent without approval0
WCAG, light + dark themeAA
Problem

Attacks now happen outside the firewall

Attackers copy a brand’s site, logo and people on the open internet, where security tools can’t see.

  • Phishing sites
  • Brand misuse
  • Fake social accounts
  • Fake executives
  • Leaked logins
  • Fake apps & ads

Monitir’s bet

Agents do the work, you make the call

  1. 01
    Watch for threats

    Scans domains, socials and app stores, 24/7

    Done by Agents
  2. →
  3. 02
    Investigate each one

    Collects proof and scores confidence

    Done by Agents
  4. →
  5. 03
    Take the decision

    Approves or rejects the drafted action

    Done by You
  6. →
  7. 04
    Remove & follow up

    Sends the takedown, checks it stays down

    Done by Agents

The real problem

Not finding threats, but knowing which to act on

  • NoiseToo many false alerts#1 complaint about DRP tools on G2
  • Trust“Will AI act without me?”A wrong takedown is on the Security Lead
  • Time to valueWeeks before it helps1–2 months to set up, say reviewers
How might we

Get a Security Lead to a confident first decision in minutes, and keep them in control at 100× volume?

Design principles

Five rules every screen had to pass

  1. Decisions, not alertsGroup the noise
    FixesFalse positives
  2. Show the workEvery AI claim has proof
    FixesDoubt in AI
  3. Nothing leaves without youAgents draft, you approve
    FixesFear of autonomy
  4. Value before setup endsFirst scan in minutes
    FixesSlow rollouts
  5. Earn the habit5-min check, Friday brief
    FixesManual reports

Who does what

After Alex taps Approve

  1. 1YouReview the evidence and tap Approve
  2. 2YouConfirm. 8 seconds to undo
  3. 3AgentsSend the request to registrar and host
  4. 43rd partyRegistrar & web host take the fake page down
  5. 5AgentsChase replies, then verify with 3 clean checks

What I learned, what I’d do next

Learnings

  1. 01

    Trust is the UX

    Show proof, scope and undo before asking for a click.

  2. 02

    Empty states speak loudest

    “Preparing” beats “0 threats”.

  3. 03

    Scale changes the unit

    Past a point, people need campaigns, not rows.

  4. 04

    Cutting is design

    I dropped a “time saved” card no one could verify.

Next

  1. 01

    Test with 5–6 Security Leads

  2. 02

    Approve from Slack, Teams, mobile

  3. 03

    Role views: Legal, IT, CISO

  4. 04

    Test if confidence scores help

  5. 05

    Lift chart colours to 3:1 contrast
